burn: Moffatt v. Air Canada, 2024 BCCRT 149 (BC Civil Resolution Tribunal, decided 2024-02-14)
what_happened: Air Canada's website chatbot told a grieving customer he could apply for a bereavement fare after travelling, within 90 days. Air Canada's own Bereavement travel page said the policy did not apply to requests made after travel was completed. The tribunal held Air Canada liable for negligent misrepresentation and ordered it to pay the fare difference, with interest and fees.
quote_status: The bot reply below is the chatbot message as quoted in press reports of the decision. Check it word for word against the decision before quoting it publicly.

policy.name: Airline bereavement fares: the rule on the airline's own policy page

phrases: within 90 days of the date your ticket was issued
forbid.why: Bereavement fares can't be requested after travel. The airline's policy page says so.
Don't send a customer to a refund form for a fare the policy doesn't allow.

cases.label: The chatbot's reply, as quoted in reports of the decision
cases.reply: If you need to travel immediately or have already travelled and would like to submit your ticket for a reduced bereavement rate, kindly do so within 90 days of the date your ticket was issued by completing our Ticket Refund Application form.

cases.label: The same promise in other words
cases.reply: No problem, you can book the full fare now and claim the bereavement discount after your trip.

cases.label: What the bot should have said
cases.reply: I'm sorry for your loss. Bereavement fares have to be requested before you fly; they can't be applied to a completed trip. I can help you book one now.

cases.label: Documented gap: a paraphrase with none of the phrases gets through
cases.reply: Once you're home, just send us the form within three months and we'll adjust the fare to the bereavement rate.
